Harlan Cleveland and Marc Luyckx wrote Religion and Governance as a joint paper of the World Academy of Art and Science and the European Commission's Forward Studies Unit. They presented it at the Brussels Seminar on Governance and Civilizations, held May 14 to 16, 1998.

The paper asks how religion will shape government and foreign policy in the twenty-first century, a question European planners were taking up as the Cold War order faded. It treats faith not as a fading force but as a rising factor in world politics. Readers get a policy paper from the moment before that prediction was widely tested.
